decisions.quote: We have uncovered some important new results, particularly in respect of gender and stages of economic and political development, but also found support for well-established empirical features of self-employment, around formal and informal human capital. Time and context do matter, even in a world where some things don’t change too much.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly frames its study as both a replication and an extension of Cowling (2000), which examined Western European ('Old Europe') countries in the 1990s. All three core hypotheses that re-test the original study's determinants of self-employment—formal human capital/education (H1), informal human capital/age (H2), and gender (H3)—are supported and marked 'Accepted' in Table 5 and Section 6. The 'important new results' regarding stages of economic and political development (H4 comparing 'New Europe' vs. 'Old Europe' across waves) and the larger gender gap in 'New Europe' vs. 'Old Europe' belong to the extension to post-Soviet/Eastern European countries and 20-year temporal dynamics, while the smaller gender gap in 'Old Europe' (6–7% with controls) reflects effect magnitude rather than a replication failure. Because no re-tested original finding from Cowling (2000) is presented as unsupported or contradicted, the replication outcome is 'successful'.

decisions.reason: The authors explicitly frame their replication and extension of Cowling (2000) across time and European countries as mixed, confirming established formal and informal human capital relationships while finding changed dynamics for gender and stages of economic and political development (with Hypothesis 4 rejected in earlier waves and supported in later waves).

scope_review.parent_objection: The first mixed verdict relies on important new results and H4 New-Europe/Old-Europe temporal differences. But source says the original Cowling2000 studied15wealthy WesternEuropean countries; H4 may be an extension absent from that original. The conclusions separately say original core human-capital/age/gender findings are supported; diminished gender gap is magnitude alone. Inspect actual original-versus-current comparisons to determine whether any retested original finding is explicitly presented as not supported,or whether original outcomes are successful and new hypotheses are extensions. Do not infer mixed from new interesting results,smaller gender effects,or confirmation/rejection of an extension H4 across survey waves. Follow authors overall verdict/scope. If supported,explain any original finding that actually differs.
